title: Set up mailing address
summary: Choose a business address suitable for the company’s legal, banking and mail-handling needs. Complete the applicable address and mail-receipt authorizations, verify that correspondence reaches the company and update the relevant records.

parts.title: Choose mailing address provider
parts.guidance: Decide whether the address must support forwarding, scanning, parcels or specific bank or agency uses. Check that those institutions accept the proposed address type, then compare privacy controls, handling limits, location and charges. Choose who may access scanned mail and approve a suitable plan. An address useful for correspondence may still be unsuitable for another required address field.

execution.rationale: Compare address acceptance, handling limits and privacy controls against the intended correspondence uses.

parts.title: Sign up and pick an address plan
parts.guidance: Select the location and plan based on expected scanning, forwarding and storage. Review cancellation terms and register the company and authorized recipients accurately. The account holder approves the subscription and required identity disclosures. Configure access and urgent-notice routing, and use the provider’s exact address format once its onboarding requirements are complete and service is active.

execution.rationale: The applicant chooses and activates the address plan in the provider's digital account process; the later witnessed mail authorization remains separate.

parts.title: Fill out the provider's mail-handling authorization
parts.guidance: Complete the authorization the postal rules require with the applicant, company, address and authorized recipients. Follow the accepted identity and address-document requirements through the provider’s secure process. Resolve inaccurate or missing fields before the applicant completes the live signature-witnessing step. Keep the identity documents and prepared application private.

geoResolutions.label: The authorization is the current USPS Form 1583; the CMRA keeps it on file

execution.rationale: Stable, Earth Class Mail and VirtualPostMail document online form preparation using company, recipient and identification details. Their browser flows support preparing or correcting the authorization before the separate witnessing step. The applicant supplies personal identity evidence and completes any selfie or identity challenge; approval and secure handling remain required.

parts.title: Sign the mail authorization with the witnessing the rules require
parts.guidance: Use the witnessing route the provider and the applicable postal rules support. The applicant completes that process with the required IDs. Resolve any provider rejection before treating the mail authorization as active.

verify.how: The provider accepts the completed mail-handling authorization and activates the address; retain the executed form, which the provider keeps on file.

geoResolutions.label: Form 1583 permits signature or confirmation before the agent or authorized employee, or acknowledgement before a qualifying notary, with the specified physical or live virtual presence

execution.rationale: Use an in-person witnessing route with the applicant's IDs and signature. Provider acceptance and any supported remote alternative remain separate checks.

parts.title: Update the address on file (bank, tax authority, vendors)
parts.guidance: Identify where the old address appears and distinguish mailing, physical, registered-office and tax fields. Check each institution’s accepted address types and update method. Authorized account holders submit the changes and verify important notices reach the new destination. Maintain old-mailbox access or forwarding during the transition, and resolve any institution that rejects the new address type.

execution.rationale: The administrator coordinates address changes with banks, authorities and vendors through their account or correspondence channels, checking address-type rules and arranging mail continuity separately.

metadata.supportReason: Signup is an online form; USPS Form 1583 needs a notarized founder signature — genuinely human.

geoNotes.summary: Virtual-office addresses are a normal, legal registered-office choice — but post-ECCT the address must be one where documents actually come to the company's attention, and Companies House now also requires a registered email address.

The registered office is declared to the MCA (INC-22, within 30 days of incorporation where not declared at filing) and every change files back to the RoC; virtual-office addresses are widely used — including per-state for GST registrations, each state wanting its own proof-of-address set.

The company's inländische Geschäftsanschrift lives in the Handelsregister and the website's Impressum needs a ladungsfähige Anschrift — a business-center address is fine if post genuinely reaches you; address changes go through the notary to the register, so pick one that will last.

Domiciliation is its own regulated service in France: a société de domiciliation (agréée by the préfecture) contracts to host your siège social, and the address flows through the INPI guichet unique onto the RCS — the service-public page is the canonical map of what qualifies.

The sede registered in the commercial registry is where official mail and service arrive — a business-center or virtual-office address is legitimate if post genuinely reaches the company, and changes are filed online.

The registered office must be a street address in the incorporating jurisdiction where documents can be served — virtual-office providers are a normal choice as long as mail reliably reaches the company, with changes filed online.

The registered office must be a Singapore address open and accessible to the public during normal business hours each business day (law rule sg.registered-office-requirement) — a corporate service provider's registered-office service is the standard startup answer.

The registered office must be an Australian address where communications reliably reach the company, with the occupier's consent recorded when the company is not the occupier — service providers' registered-office addresses are a normal choice, and changes are notified to ASIC within 28 days.
The company’s official address is the seat of the principal office in the articles and the registry; moving it is a registrable change on the two-week clock (Commercial Act Article 183).

The registered office must be in Hong Kong and able to receive all communications and notices (law rule hk.registered-office-requirement); it is stated on the incorporation form, changes file within 15 days, and a corporate service provider's registered-office service is the standard startup answer.

The company's official address lives in the commercial register and changes through the e-Business Register; a company with a foreign address must keep an Estonian contact person for service of documents (law rule ee.management-board-contact-person).
